subject: dwarfRifleman
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf rifleman with braided beard and blunderbuss.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm designing a chunky Warcraft-style dwarf rifleman with pauldrons, braided beard, and a blunderbuss, planning out the skeleton structure with hips as root, spine chain, neck, and head joints at dwarf proportions around 1.3 meters tall.

Still writing joint hierarchy...

Defining torso stations for a wide dwarf build, giving pelvis, waist, chest, and shoulders their own widths and depths. For the head I'm placing a scaled sphere with a bulbous nose, brow ridge box, and simple plane-based eyes.

Now I'm positioning dark eye decals on the skull surface and planning a steel dome helmet with a brim, leaving the brow and face unobstructed. Writing lathe outline coordinates...

For the beard, I'm lofting a big orange-red wedge shape from chin down, rigidly attached to the head bone, with braids made from stacked spheres along a path, plus curving moustache capsules on each side.

Now I'm working out the arm chains and shoulder-elbow positions, deciding on a neutral A-pose with arms slightly extended, and figuring out how the blunderbuss should be rigidly attached to one hand bone.

Defining the gun geometry now, with the grip positioned at the wrist and the barrel built as a tapered lathe shape running along the direction from butt to muzzle, parented to the hand joint.

Adding gun lock and trigger guard details, then moving to the legs: setting hip, knee, and ankle joints with leg radius tapering down to boot boxes with darker soles, making sure the boot bottom sits flush at y=0. Then sketching out the tunic and belt approach using a torso loft.

Now I'm working out the belt as a swept loop around the hip joint, plus a buckle part, and designing a bandolier as a draped curve across the chest from the right shoulder to the left hip using a catmull path with control points through the front and back.

I'm adding cartridge pouches distributed along that path as small cylinders with brass tips using a path-sampling helper, then shifting focus to pauldrons—oversized iron spheres scaled and positioned on the shoulder joints with brass studs and a gold trim torus, tied into the shoulder bone chain for the arm sweep.

Now I'm defining the arm chain with four named joints (shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand) for three spans, using polyline sweeps for crisp joints rather than smoothed catmull curves, with a tapering radius array and sphere-capped hand tips and gauntlet cuffs at the wrists.

For textures, I'm planning an eye decal and a rune/emblem design to place on the tabard, belt buckle, and pauldron, along with a cloth pattern. I'm working out the tabard as a textured plane hanging from the belt with a thin extruded outline border for depth, considering whether to extrude the shape directly or layer a textured plane over a colored box base.

Working out the tabard's extruded shape and positioning relative to the torso's depth at the hips and chest, adjusting the z-offset and thickness so it sits properly against the belt area without clipping into the body.

I'll keep the color palette modest using paint helper functions for countershading, grain, and mottling effects, limiting flat colors to 64 or fewer -- using grain along the y-axis for the beard's two-tone browns and a tan tone for the skin.

Now I'm working out head geometry: positioning the head sphere, cheeks, nose, and brow as small primitives relative to the head center, with eye decals projected onto the curved front surface so they sit flush with the sphere's radius at that height.

For the jaw and mouth, I'm placing a separate scaled sphere at the chin for the lower jaw (so it can move independently for speech), attaching the beard geometry to this jaw bone, keeping the moustache on the main head, and adding a small dark box for the mouth opening hidden beneath the facial hair.

Now I'm working out the helmet geometry using a lathe profile positioned above the head, calculating the dome radius and rim height based on the head's curvature at the brow line so it fits snugly before building out the top of the dome.

Adding swept-back horns from the sides of the helmet and a crest ridge fin extruded along the top for a dwarf warrior look.

Now I'm thinking about accessories like a powder horn, bedroll, and satchel on the hips and back to keep the character grounded, plus figuring out how to position the gun in the right hand so it passes naturally through the grip at the wrist.

Still defining barrel geometry...

Now I'm adding flintlock details -- lock plate, hammer, pan brass on the side, plus a trigger guard torus, skipping the sling strap since the gun rigging is fine. I'm also considering adding a small glowing amber lantern hanging at the hip for extra atmosphere, checking the glow kit import path.

For footwear I'm building leather boots with a cuffed roll-over top and brass buckle, sizing the shaft cylinder to cover the lower leg and attaching it along the leg bone chain between the ankle joint and tip.

Defining leg and foot geometry...

Now I'm setting up the spine chain as a skinned torso loft with joints for spine1, spine2, and chest, planning to parent the arms off the chest joint and the neck off the spine tip, with hips as the root joint.

I'm then defining the neck chain extending from the chest to a neck tip, with a head joint parented off that for aiming dir forward, plus a short sweep skin covering the neck that's mostly hidden by a beard, and now working out how the jaw should aim relative to the head joint.

For the torso I'm building a loft across stations bound to the hips/spine chain, sizing the chest width and checking how the shoulder pauldron placement matches a broad dwarf build, then setting up the tunic coloring with a blue-and-gold Ironforge palette using mottled paint for the coat.

Now I'm planning the tabard: leather coat, blue tunic with gold trim, steel armor accents, and a gold emblem resembling a hammer-and-anvil rune. I'm sketching the emblem as an SVG banner shape with a blue field and gold border, thinking through using a textured plane with alpha cutout for the tabard outline, needing front and back planes since only one side would otherwise show.

Working through placement details for the front and back tabard planes, then moving on to the eye SVG design—almond white shape with a dark outline, blue iris, pupil and highlight—plus bushy dwarf brows as angled capsules and a mustache shape to match.

Now I'm defining the beard's loft stations down the jawline, tapering width and height from chin to chest, checking it doesn't clash with the torso geometry, then starting on the side braids.

Adding helper functions for building spheres and pauldrons—using a scaled sphere for the shoulder dome with a gold torus ring at its base, and planning small stud spheres arranged around the ring.

Still working out the arm joint structure...

Hanging the lantern near the belt on the left hip with a small glowing cylinder, brass cap, and hook, then adding a powder horn on the right hip using a tapered bezier sweep, and starting a bedroll cylinder across the back for the backpack.

Now sketching out the bag box, deciding to skip the keg and cape, and setting up paint definitions and material imports (builder, frame helpers, bezier/catmull curves, mottling, grain, countershading) along with a vector helper and lathe geometry for the muzzle before defining decal placement for the skull emblem.

I'm figuring out the head geometry — a scaled skin sphere for the head, cheek and ear spheres, and a jaw ball positioned under the face. I'm deciding to skip teeth and mouth detail since the moustache and beard will cover that area anyway.

Now I'm setting up the torso and leg construction: a colored loft for the torso and a leather-brown sweep for the pant legs, with the hip radius tapering down. I'm also designing a tabard SVG pennant shape with a blue fill and gold stroke, adding a simple anvil/hammer and crossed-rifle emblem, rasterized at 192px.

Sizing out the tabard plane geometry so it drapes correctly between the belt and knees without clipping the thigh radius, then writing out the final code carefully.
